title: Software & Engineering Projects
description: Applied engineering work spanning robotics perception, on-device inference, and LLM-powered tooling — from prototype to measured benchmark.

items.title: 3D Mapping Using a Mechanically Oscillating 2D LiDAR
items.description: Built a sub-$150 3D scanner by mounting an RPLIDAR C1 on an oscillating MG996R servo, tagging each 2D scan with its tilt angle and reassembling slices into ROS2 PointCloud2 maps. Compared servo-commanded (open-loop) and MPU6050 IMU-assisted (closed-loop) tilt estimation, achieving 9.1 mm plane-fit RMSE on a flat-wall test; extended the pipeline with Poisson surface meshing and a monocular depth (Depth-Anything-V2) baseline for cross-modal comparison.

items.title: Toward On-Device Mosquito Larvae Identification: Lightweight Blur-Robust Classifiers with INT8/INT4 Quantization
items.description: Trained MobileNetV3-Small, EfficientNet-Lite0, and MobileViT-S on the MosquitoLarvae-7400 benchmark (7,463 images, 4 species) using a two-stage regimen and a blur / motion-blur / colour-jitter augmentation pipeline. Exported each model to ONNX and evaluated FP32, static INT8, and weight-only INT4 through real ONNX Runtime sessions. EfficientNet-Lite0 gave the best accuracy–robustness trade-off (99.73% clean / 98.66% blurred) and was the only model viable under static INT8 (96.50% at 3.5× compression). All variants benchmarked end-to-end on PC and Android via onnxruntime-web WASM.

items.title: AI-Based Diabetes Diagnosis System
items.description: An end-to-end AI system for diabetes diagnosis that combines predictive machine learning with conversational LLM assistance for comprehensive patient assessment. Deliberately lightweight — runs on a budget GPU with 8 GB of VRAM.
items.highlight: A portion of this work was accepted at IEEE iCONEECT.

items.title: Localized RAG Pipeline for Cisco IOS Configuration Generation
items.description: Designed an offline retrieval-augmented generation pipeline that produces Cisco IOS CLI commands from natural language using ChromaDB and sentence-transformer embeddings. Created a validated dataset of 2,254 QA pairs and benchmarked seven small language models (Mistral, Qwen3, Gemma) using custom metrics. Mistral achieved a 51% exact match, demonstrating practical, privacy-preserving local network automation.
